lines.en: label makotospecial50:
scene unbluejay1
Redbirds bleed and blue ones die — that’s the nature of this world of mine.
The green ones sing, the yellows cry — yet still the redbirds bleed. But why?
I close my book. Breathe out a sigh. Then pierce the glass with both my eyes.
Approach the window, scan the sky — beneath the clouds, above the pines.
The blue ones fall as the red ones rise. Don’t ask me how, I won’t reply.
I can’t tell you why the cardinals fly. I can’t tell you why the blues won’t try.
I can’t tell you anything as I-
I hate this fucking world of mine.
I hate the birds. I hate the sky. I hate paper, pencils, crooked lines.
These are reasons why I sometimes try imagining that I am blind.
I know there’s beauty here.
There has to be.
It’s just way too hard to find.
: Helloooo? Senseiiiii? Did you forget that you’re supposed to be working right now?
: Forget? No. Ignore? Yes.
: Well, on the bright side, you’re almost done. I just need your signature on a few more forms and you can go back to being irresponsible and lazy like you always are.
: Why haven’t you just started forging my signature on everything yet? That would save both of us so much time.
: Because I’m honest. Which is also why I don’t mind admitting that these paper-relays of ours are some of the very few moments we share that actually count as bonding in my book.
: Does it not count as bonding when I put my penis inside of you?
: It used to. Now, that’s more akin to something like cracking my knuckles or yawning. Just a standard bodily function. The novelty has worn off.
: What am I even signing anyway? Why are there so many more sheets of paper than normal?

: Because you have twenty different students who all just finished their standardized tests — which, and this may come as a big surprise to you, are a little more in-depth than just one sheet of paper.
: I don’t know if I believe you. I feel like you might just be handing me blank sheets of paper in order to pad the numbers of our “bonding time.”
scene unbluejay2
: Are you seriously not even looking at them? They’re very clearly not blank.
: They look blank to me. But that’s probably just because I’ve gotten so used to tuning everything out that the words don’t even register anymore.
: That is both very sad and very impressive. I wish I could care as little as you.
: You did for a little while. What happened to that Makoto? How do we bring her back?
scene unbluejay3
: Easy! By killing someone else who’s important to me.
: Pass. Too much effort. Also, your mom would have been proud of that joke.
scene unbluejay4
: Ahh, my poor mother...I remember her like it was yesterday. What a shame that she, too-
: I’m glad you’re feeling better, Makoto.
scene unbluejay5
: Huh?
: I said I’m glad you’re feeling better.
: Are you saying that because you mean it? Or because you think I’ll take it easy on you and let you finish signing things early because you showed me the slightest bit of sentimentality?
: ...Both?
scene unbluejay6
: Just sign the last few papers, Sensei. We’re almost done.
: I will sign one more. The rest can wait until tomorrow. My hand hurts.
: Just one? Really?
: Choose wisely, Makoto. Whose grades matter the most?
scene unbluejay7
: Hmm...just one, huh?
: But there are at least eighty more that need to be signed.
: I thought you said we were-
scene unbluejay8
: Here! Sign this one!
: Final answer?
: Final answer.
scene unbluejay9
I take the “final” paper from Makoto and, after looking at it for almost a full second, I spot her name and realize that there was really only one option available to her in the first place.
Then, as I sign my name along the bottom section of the document, I silently applaud her for her selfishness as it is one of several things we have in common.
The other things being poor vision and a burning passion for rough sex — even if she claims it isn’t much of a big deal anymore.
: Okay. Done.
scene unbluejay10
: Thank you for your service.
: It was hard, but I’m glad we made it through the day.
scene unbluejay11
: It’s been approximately fifteen minutes since I came in here.
: Yeah, but you were there for the rest of the day so the statement stands. But anyway, what now? Want to engage in “bodily functions” on the couch?
: That sounded absolutely disgusting even if I knew what you meant.
: Yeah, I’m sorry.
scene unbluejay12
: Would it be selfish of me to ask if I can have you for a little while longer?
: Yes. But I was actually just thinking about how I like your selective brand of selfishness, so go ahead and have me. But I’d still prefer the couch over-
scene unbluejay13
: Not here.
: There’s somewhere else I want to go.
scene black
scene unbluejay14
It becomes fairly evident that Makoto was asking to “have” me in a more hands-free sort of way the moment we make it up to the rooftop.
Either that or she’s just into the same sort of stuff Ayane is. Which, honestly, wouldn’t be all that surprising since Ayane’s only fetish seems to just be me as a whole.
The air is warm, but not warm enough to make me regret coming out here. It’s one of those days where you’re acutely aware that it is summer, but...
Well, if I didn’t know any better, I’d say this is a little closer to spring.
Makoto skips closer to the fence, causing her skirt to bounce along with her “perverted adjective, followed by perverted noun.”
And, in other news, signing so many papers in one sitting has drained the last bit of motivation I have left in my body.
It is all downhill from here.
: This weather’s amazing, isn’t it? And the sky is so bright.
: It’s probably symbolism.
scene unbluejay15
: Is it? For what?
: Maybe this...newer...bubbly front you’re putting on.
: It’s not a front, Sensei.
: The skies are just starting to clear up a little.
: I knew it was symbolism. I told you.
: I will take that as a passing grade on this impromptu weather-based and somewhat-literary evaluation test. Thank you very much.
: Let’s hope it lasts this time and that no further tragedy follows the customarily tragic life of Makoto Miyamura.
scene unbluejay16
: Even if it does, I think I’ll be fine.
: The worst has passed. Things couldn’t possibly be that bad ever again without me losing a child or something. And I’m not even sure if I want kids.
: You don’t.
: You’re only saying that because you don’t want kids.
: Why would I ever say anything that doesn’t directly relate to me? That just sounds like a waste of time.
: Narcissism and uncertain futures aside, I hope you’re right. I’ve had enough tragedy for one school year.
: Actually, I’ve probably had enough for my entire high school career. So yeah, let’s hang it up for now.
: Back to the original plan then? Working hard and just doing your own thing with little regard for your own sanity and how everyone else feels about you?
: Maybe.
: I’m trying not to think about it.
: I just kind of want to exist right now.
scene black
: And whatever that entails is fine by me.
: Makoto? Where are you going?
: Hm? Higher. To get a better view of the city.
: Want to follow me up? Or would you rather stay down there on the ground like a pansy?
Being an alpha-male who is most assuredly not a “pansy,” I follow Makoto up the ladder until we’re level with the fence...
scene unbluejay17
A fall from this high up would certainly kill us, and I need to think for a moment about whether or not my incessant beratement of Makoto would prompt her to end my life.
: I’m really happy you’re here, Sensei.
She attempts to lure me into a false sense of security.
: Is that only because you brought me up here to murder me?
I subtly let her know that I’m onto her.
: No. It’s because there’s no one I’d rather look out over this horizon with than you.
: It feels almost nostalgic in a way, doesn’t it?
: Well, yeah. We’ve been up here before.
: That was a long time ago, though.
: A lot has happened since then, huh?
: More than you know, Makoto.
: Do you think I’ll make a good teacher one day?
: I think you make a good teacher right now. I worry about how “good” you’ll be once you’re done with college.
: I really hope I can be like you one day. Just without all of the statutory rape. And lack of motivation. And built-in cynicism.
: So basically, you just want to have my job title.
: And the ability to motivate people. Yes.
: I don’t motivate anyone, Makoto.
scene unbluejay18
: You don’t try to motivate anyone. But the weird and unfortunate truth is that you unintentionally do.
: Though, I guess it’s possible that we’re all so desperate to end up as someone unlike you that seeing you struggle gets us to “wake up.”
: Have we entered the arc where you bully me now?
scene unbluejay19
: Possibly. All things considered, I’m definitely not the same girl I was the last time we were up here.
: What kind of girl that makes me, I have no idea. But I know I’ve gotta get it together if I want to keep looking up at the clouds like this.
: For a while, well before everything with my dad happened, the sky lost its color. It was this...huge blanket of gray that made everything beneath it look lifeless and dull.
: I thought about leaving a ton of times.
: I went as far as writing notes. To you. To my mom. To Miku. I even wrote one to Ami once — but even that was mostly about you.
: Makoto-
: I thought about coming up here, throwing myself off of this roof, and letting life move on without me because I just didn’t have what it takes to keep going.
scene unbluejay20
: I still think about it sometimes.
: About what would have happened if I had followed through.
: I think about what would happen to my mom and the store.
: I think about what would happen to Miku’s grades.
: Or if you’d blame yourself for it even though it was never your fault.
: This is the way I’ve always been. And hey, maybe I’ll be this way forever — never totally sure of whether or not there’s a purpose out there for someone like me.
: But that’s okay...because I know the end of my suffering would just spell more suffering for all of those people I wrote to.
: So one of my new goals is to prevent anyone I care about from ever having to read anything like that.
: I don’t want anyone else to ever have to feel the way I do.
scene unbluejay21
: Sorry...that probably wasn’t as happy of an ending as you were hoping for, was it?
: No, it really wasn’t...
: I expected something more along the lines of “I want to be here now because I’ve found what it means to be happy” or whatever.
: That sure would be nice, wouldn’t it?
: And...who knows? Maybe some day, I’ll be able to think that way. But for now-
: You just want to exist.
scene unbluejay22
: That’s right...
: But in a way, for someone who’s always setting the bar so high, maybe a little goal like this will be easier for me to climb over?
: I have no one to succeed for anymore other than myself.
: If I look at it that way, I won’t have to push myself so hard.
: And if I don’t push myself so hard, I’ll have more time to focus on what I know matters more than anything else.
: And that is?
: Not writing any more notes.
: And learning how to smile from the bottom of my heart instead of the pit of my stomach.
: I’m really happy you’re here, Makoto.
scene unbluejay23
: Hey. That was my line. You can’t just go plagiarizing me as soon as there’s an awkward silence.
: Sure I can. And until you’re the one in my position, you can’t tell me what to do.
scene unbluejay24
: I can’t?
: You can’t.
: Bummer.
: Can I at least ask for a little favor, though?
: I’m done grading papers until tomorrow.
: It’s not that. It’s something else.
: What is it?
scene black
: Can you close your eyes for a second?
scene unbluejay25
Redbirds bleed and blue ones die — that’s the nature of this world of mine.
There’s no song to sing nor hymn to cry — just an aching heart and wat’ry eyes.
I hate love and lust and God and lies. I hate hummingbirds. The word “Goodbye.”
But if you’d ask me now, beneath this sky-
I could tell you why the cardinals fly.
scene black
